sentences.text: JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 18.12.2023 at about 7.45 a.m. the petitioner was riding her Yamaha fashion scooter bearing registration No.KA-05-JV-9289 on CT Bed road,
Channammanakere Achukattu, BSK 2 nd Stage, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05-JC-3295 rode the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Atreum Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she was treated as an inpatient and had spent huge amount towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 46 years, Dentist at Dr.Dinakar's Smile Dental Care,
Bengtaluru and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month and she used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of her family members.
After the accident, she could not do any work due to her severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-05-JC-3295.
In this regard, case was registered against the rider by the jurisdictional Police in Crime No.608/2023 under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondent.

In response to the notices,
the respondent has appeared through his counsel, but inspite of sufficient opportunities given to him has not filed his written statement.
Therefore, written statement of the respondent is taken as not filed.
7. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Ramesh as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.

Further examined EMO as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.
8.
Inspite of giving sufficient opportunities sufficient opportunities to the respondent, neither cross examined the PW1 nor adduced any oral or documentary evidence on his behalf.

On the basis of rival pleadings, the Points that would arise for consideration are as under:
POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, she had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, that was taken place on 18.12.2023 at about 7.45 a.m. near C.T.Channammanakere Achukattu BSK 2nd stage, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05-JC- 3295, in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

from whom?
3) What order or award?

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
11.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S POINT NO.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05- JC-3295, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.
13.
On the other hand, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle has appeared before the court but not filed his written statement.
In such a situation, duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence placed by the petitioner in support of the above fact in issue.
14. The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

sentences.text: On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Devaraj C., the S.H.O. of Banashankari Traffic Police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and under Section 134(a & b) , 187, 3(1), 181, 146 and 196 of IMV Act.
16 . All these material documents which indicate against the guilt of actionable negligence committed by the rider of the offending vehicle remained unquestioned.
At the outset, it is to be noted that,
affidavit
evidence and the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner in connection with the above point remained unshaken and uncontroverted by the other side.

Hence, I am of the view that,
the petitioner has placed satisfactory and convincing evidence, to prove the above point to the effect that, the alleged accident was occurred purely on the part of the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05-JC- 3295 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries. Accordingly, I am answering the Point No.1 is in the Affirmative.
POINT NO.2 :
17. This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

18. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P12 issued by Atreum Specialityl hospital which reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 18.12.2023 to 23.12.2023.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Ramesh as PW2.

He has placed outpatient record and x-ray as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an inpatient as well as an outpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
21.
PW1 has stated that, she is a Dental Practitioiner at Dr.Dinakar's Smile Dental Care, Bengaluru and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
In support of her case, she has not placed any single documents to show that she is a Dental Practioner and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
In the absence of any documents with regard to her avocation and income, it is apt to be considered notional income.
On going through the discharge summary as per Ex.P12 issued by Atreum Specialityl hospital which reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 18.12.2023 to 23.12.2023.
During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.
Hence, I am of the view that,
it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
22.
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills as per Ex.P13 to the extent of Rs.2,09,087/-.
There are no any contradictions to disbelieve the medical bills as the respondent remained as silent spectator in this case.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,09,087/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
23.
As per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient.

During that period, definitely the petitioner might have spent Sujatha N vs Maheshwara T on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9508999/
5 some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained by the petitoner, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
24.
The petitioner herein asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by her as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, she had sustained grievous injuries, for which she took the treatment as inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Ramesh examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg.
The petitioner treated with internal fixation of tibia and fibula.
He has placed outpatient record and x-ray, which are marked as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.

Further PW2 has assessed the disability of 28% of left lower limb and whole body disability is 14%.
25.

PW1 has stated that she was working is a Dental Practitioner at Dr.Dinakar's Smile Dental Care,
Bengaluru and was drawing salary of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Further petitioner has not placed any documents to show that whether she has continued her job or quit her job because of the accidental injuries.
In the absence of any documents, it is to be considered that the petitioner is continuing her service as usual.
26. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.
At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to her to do normal work, as she was earlier.

Hence, I relied the decision reported in, ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, it was observed,
that.

sentences.text: "The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.
The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

sentences.text: On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

28. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued her job, she has to suffer with the said disability throughout her life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.

Loss of amenities;
29.
As noted above, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident as a result she has permanent partial disability.
The petitioner was aged about 46 years at the time of the accident.

The said disability certainly affects not only on her avocation, but also affects on her amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy her life as she was enjoying earlier prior to the accident.
By overall considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
30. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
Either the PW1 & PW2 has not placed any estimation in this regard.
But by considering her injuries, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medication.
31. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:

20,000-00 6 Future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.4,31,087-00 32.

sentences.text:
LIABILITY:
33.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05-JC- 3295, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in this regard remained unshaken.
As per the documentary evidence, the owner of the offending vehicle had no valid insurance policy and also not having valid driving license, as on the date of the accident.
As such, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
Resultantly, I am answering the point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

POINT NO.3:
34.

In view of above discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,31,087/- (Rupees four lakh thirty one thousand and eighty seven only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till its realisation.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
